title: Drift-Aware Memory-Augmented Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention for Industrial Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Reliable anomaly detection is needed for industrial control systems whose data are high-dimensional multivariate time series with complex spatio-temporal dependencies and non-stationary device behaviors.

gap.claim: Existing graph and temporal modeling approaches limit long-range reasoning and assume static spatio-temporal reliability, an assumption that breaks under temporal drift.

contributions.claim: DRAMA is a drift-aware, memory-augmented spatio-temporal attention framework for anomaly detection in non-stationary industrial control systems.
The framework combines topology-guided and similarity-aware spatial attention with explicit memory retrieval for long-range device-level context.
It estimates device-wise drift from memory trajectories and adaptively reweights spatial and temporal evidence to emphasize stable signals and suppress volatility-induced noise.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets reportedly show improvements in detection accuracy, temporal consistency, and anomaly localization under non-stationarity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Industrial control systems face cyber-physical attacks and require reliable anomaly detection.
Industrial control system data contain high-dimensional multivariate signals with complex dependencies and non-stationary behavior.
Existing methods use restrictive graph and temporal assumptions that fail when temporal drift changes device dynamics and dependency reliability.
DRAMA addresses the gap with drift-aware attention, memory-based long-range context, and adaptive evidence weighting.
The authors report improved detection accuracy, temporal consistency, and anomaly localization on four real-world datasets under non-stationarity.

source_observation.claim: Temporal drift can change both device-level dynamics and the relative reliability of local temporal and cross-device evidence.

interpretation.claim: Anomaly detectors for non-stationary systems may need reliability-aware adaptation rather than fixed dependency assumptions.

application.claim: Use drift estimates to adaptively weight spatial and temporal signals in monitoring systems with changing operating conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy improves performance outside the reported industrial control system settings.

unknowns: Dataset identities and characteristics are not specified.
Baseline methods, metric definitions, quantitative improvements, and experimental protocol are not specified.
The memory mechanism and drift-estimation procedure are not described in implementation detail.
